top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P003) remains my first choice on the common criteria. Her voice is spare, ironic and exact, and it is recognizable across Autobiography of Red, Nox and the essays such as Eros the Bittersweet. Her formal invention is exceptional. Concerns of grief, desire, the fragment and the afterlife of ancient texts recur across forms, which I read as development and not repetition. Her English text can be tested directly by the committee, though I treat that as an evidentiary advantage and not as merit. The citation can stay on her own poetry and essays, so the book-object elements of Nox and Float need not carry the claim. I hold this with less certainty than in round 1: I cannot show that quality is even across her smaller books, and I have not independently verified the corpus. Cărtărescu (P001) is a close second. His cumulative prose architecture is a serious case, the narrowed prose-centred citation is defensible, and the unverified questions of translation loss and evenness in the late novels apply to him as much as to the others. Adonis (P002) is third. His remaking of Arabic poetic language is a major achievement, but I cannot assess the Arabic prosody or the later collections except through translation. That is an evidentiary limit, not a judgment against him. P000 is last because I do not find the evidence for any of the three leading candidates so thin that no award is warranted.
